title: Generalized Fidelity and the Data Processing Inequality
abstract: In this note, we show that the generalized Bures--Wasserstein distance induced by the generalized fidelity does not satisfy the data processing inequality in dimensions greater than two. In dimension two, although we do not settle the DPI in full generality, we derive two sufficient conditions guaranteeing it by using an explicit formula for the real part of the generalized fidelity. Furthermore, we find a necessary and sufficient condition under which the generalized fidelity reduces to the Uhlmann fidelity.
summary: This theoretical note examines the generalized Bures-Wasserstein distance derived from the generalized fidelity in quantum information. The authors prove that this distance fails the Data Processing Inequality in dimensions higher than two. For the qubit case, they establish specific sufficient conditions under which the DPI holds, providing deeper insights into quantum channel characterization.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether the generalized Bures-Wasserstein distance, induced by the generalized fidelity, satisfies the Data Processing Inequality (DPI) for quantum channels.
main_result: The distance fails to satisfy the DPI in dimensions greater than two, but sufficient conditions for the DPI are derived for the qubit case (dimension two).
method: The authors use explicit formulas for the generalized fidelity, derived using Pauli matrix representations for qubits, and construct counterexamples to test the DPI.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on quantum states represented by positive semi-definite matrices, particularly restricting the investigation to the qubit case (2x2 matrices).
key_observables: Generalized Fidelity ($F_R(P, Q)$), Squared Generalized Bures-Wasserstein Distance ($B_R(P, Q)$), and the Uhlmann fidelity ($F_U$).
important_parameters: The dimension of the system ($n$), and the specific matrices defining the generalized fidelity.
main_assumptions: The analysis provides sufficient conditions for the qubit case, but the DPI is not settled in full generality for dimension two.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the definitions for the generalized fidelity and distance. It then proves the failure of the DPI for $n \ge 3$ using counterexamples. Finally, it derives sufficient conditions for the DPI in the qubit case and determines when the generalized fidelity reduces to the Uhlmann fidelity.
why_interesting: The study of distance metrics and their monotonicity properties (like DPI) is fundamental in quantum information theory, especially when analyzing the robustness of quantum channels.
